summary: Backend-only verification of object_storage.py MongoDB fallback and /api/admin/products/upload-image endpoint. All 4/4 pytest cases pass: (1) is_configured() returns True regardless of EMERGENT_LLM_KEY, (2) put_object/get_object succeed via Emergent Managed Object Storage when key is present, (3) put_object/get_object automatically fall back to MongoDB db.object_storage_files (bson Binary) when EMERGENT_LLM_KEY is empty, retrieving bytes identically with correct content-type, (4) end-to-end admin upload: POST /api/admin/products/upload-image (admin 2FA session via contact.us@centraders.com / PIN 050499 + OTP read from admin_2fa_tokens) returns 200 with asset_id and GET /api/products/asset/{asset_id} returns the same bytes. No 503 errors observed.
critical_code_review_comments: get_object() checks MongoDB fallback FIRST even when Emergent is configured — this is fine functionally but is an extra DB round-trip for every asset read in prod. Consider checking Emergent first when key is configured, OR keeping a bool flag on the asset doc indicating backend used.

The admin upload endpoint still carries the legacy 503 branch guarded by `if not is_configured()` — since is_configured() now unconditionally returns True, that branch is dead code and can be removed for clarity.
test_credentials: admin contact.us@centraders.com / PIN 050499 (OTP read from Mongo admin_2fa_tokens)
seed_data_creation: One MongoDB object_storage_files row inserted and deleted by the fallback test. One product_asset row + one Emergent-storage object created by the upload endpoint test (not cleaned up — tiny 1x1 PNG).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Object-storage fallback is verified end-to-end. If retesting, run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_object_storage_fallback.py /app/backend/tests/test_upload_image_endpoint.py -v`. The MongoDB-fallback branch is exercised by monkeypatching EMERGENT_LLM_KEY to empty in the first test file.
